name: hirokata
description: A curated collection of Claude Code plugins for enhanced development workflows

plugins.name: software
plugins.description: Four focused skills for planning, committing and reporting on software work: an 8-phase clean architecture vocabulary for classifying tasks (categorize-task), a planner that splits a master plan into per-phase plan files organized by feature track with complexity scores (split-plan), an interactive Conventional Commits generator that groups your changes and writes the messages (conventional-commit), and a daily handoff writer that gathers the last 24 hours of pull requests, review comments, AI coding sessions and uncommitted work into one plain-language status document (daily-handoff).

plugins.name: guild
plugins.description: Continuous agent orchestration where the plugin IS a schema and a set of skills — there is no CLI. `tursodb` already executes SQL, so guild members reach the board by writing their own SQL against a guide, and the guild's rules live IN the database: CHECK constraints are the status vocabularies, VIEWS are the derived rules (the cursor, the review gate, node readiness, the board, the brief — each with ONE definition, so two members cannot get two answers), and TRIGGERS write the `event` record on every mutation. A member can forget to call a command; a member cannot bypass a trigger or a CHECK. A ticket names a required CAPABILITY rather than an agent, and the roster is not in the database at all — who exists and what each can do is the `capabilities:` frontmatter of the agent files, read at dispatch time across every subagent available to you, so writing an agent file is the whole of hiring with nothing to sync. Each requirement runs an execution graph with exactly two gates — the plan is approved before anything is built, and findings, bugs and failures are presented together as one decision after review — and it can work a shift unattended, stopping at the next gate because a gate is the one decision no subagent can make. The library is a knowledge graph: documents carry a kind — business rules, technical pages, DECISIONS, research, runbooks — and typed edges link them to the requirements, plans, tasks and bugs they describe, decide, supersede or contradict, so 'why is it like this' is a SELECT rather than an archaeology session. A trigger snapshots every rewrite, so the documentation has its own history, and two views make the library maintain itself: one reports pages whose subject moved after they were written, the other reports shipped work nobody wrote down. Every requirement documents itself — the last node of the build template is `document`. An independent QA discipline files bugs and maps risk coverage as rows. The guild deletes nothing: there is no board clear, work is retired by status, and a fresh board is a fresh database file with the old one moved aside and still readable — a global invariant reads the `deleted` events the triggers write, so a removal cannot happen quietly. The board is local by default (`tursodb`, `.guild/guild.db`), or — with `backend: kumiai` in `.guild/config.yaml` — a shared Kumiai workspace reached through the `kumiai` MCP server's typed tools, with the same views, gates and rules. Say 'check in' to start a work session, or 'work a shift' to leave it running.

plugins.name: research
plugins.description: PhD-level multi-perspective research inspired by Stanford's STORM. The 'storm research' skill orchestrates five expert persona agents (practitioner, skeptic, economist, historian, academic), maps their contradictions, synthesizes a cited briefing, and red-teams the result. Say 'storm research <topic>' to start.

plugins.name: storytelling
plugins.description: Turn any idea, pitch, update, or decision into a message that lands using six proven storytelling frameworks (Simon Sinek's Golden Circle, Minto's Pyramid Principle, the Pixar Pitch, StoryBrand, What/So What/Now What, and ABT). The 'storytelling' skill diagnoses your audience and goal, recommends the right framework, and drafts the message — in parallel across frameworks when the framing is uncertain. Each framework is also a standalone skill. Say 'help me tell the story of <X>' to start.
